title: A PLACE THAT CANNOT BE LOST

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'So the property of the Levites is redeemable - that is, a house sold in
any town they hold - and is to be returned in the Jubilee, because the
houses in the towns of the Levites are their property among the
Israelites. But the pastureland belonging to their towns must not be sold;
it is their permanent possession'" - Lev 25:33-34 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The Levites' pastureland was declared their permanent possession, never to
be sold. In a chapter all about property changing hands, here was one thing
that could never be taken away. God secured a lasting inheritance for those
who served Him.

There is a beautiful irony in this. The Levites, who owned the least, were
given a possession more secure than anyone else's. Because they belonged to
God in a special way, their inheritance was uniquely protected.

Dear friend, this points to a truth that runs right through Scripture:
those who give up much for God are never the losers. The Levites had traded
farmland for service, and God made sure their portion was secure.

The Levites' true inheritance was actually the LORD Himself. Elsewhere God
says He is their portion and their inheritance (Num 18:20). What greater
possession could there be?

For the believer, this is our reality too. The psalmist says, the LORD is
my portion; I have said I will keep His words (Ps 119:57). Whatever else we
gain or lose, God Himself is our inheritance, and He cannot be taken away.

Jesus said no one can snatch His sheep out of the Father's hand (John
10:28-29). That is a possession more permanent than any pastureland.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is God Himself my greatest treasure, or only His gifts?
2. What have I given up for God that I sometimes count as loss?
3. How secure do I feel knowing God is my inheritance?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, You Yourself are my portion and my inheritance, and no one can take
You from me. Let me treasure You above every gift You give. Amen.
